labels.notes: Target statement: one conjoined theorem for Causal.isolatedLine carrying CausallyArcConnected, CausallyOpen, CausallyPlain, StronglyCausal, StronglyCausalOpen, absolutely minimal on every open set, ¬ Tarentin, ¬ HasChronalNeighbourEverywhere, ¬ ChronalNeighbours. Causal.isolatedLine_separates (scaffold/CausalScaffold/IsolatedLineConjoined.lean:134) carries all nine (the hereditary form is the conjunct ∀ W : Opens ℝ, isolatedLine.AbsolutelyMinimalOn W) plus eleven more. It is a closed statement on ℝ with no hypothesis or instance argument, about a concrete causality, so it is not vacuous. Every conjunct is the ladder's [[property]] `lean` name for its node (checked for all 19 causality-sort nodes). AbsolutelyMinimal elaborates as Causal.Precausality.AbsolutelyMinimal isolatedLine.toPrecausality, checked by rfl in an audit probe. The three negations are genuine refutations of the library's definitions (Properties.lean:116, ChronalNeighbourBridge.lean:107, LadderLocal.lean:178). The 16 positive and 3 negative conjuncts decide all 19 causality-sort nodes. The module docstring marks no label: its only bold-backtick item is a declaration name, which does not match ledger.py's docstring_label_re (that regex needs a label prefix with a colon).

checks: 1 Layer: imports are Causal.SCOpenWithoutTarentin, Causal.ChronalTarentin, Causal.GluingModels.Minimal and Causal.Ladder.Rules. I ran tools/ladder.py model_path in memory on lean_index()['imports'] (python3 -I, from the hub root). It is None for each import, for the 64 modules of GluingModels.Minimal's closure (24 direct imports), and for the new module with its four imports added in memory. No MODEL_LAYER module is in the closure. import_chain Minimal -> Rules = [GluingModels.Minimal, HalfLitDual, Ladder.Rules]. No Causal module imports the new one, so it is a leaf with no cycle (kb/0221). grep finds no metric, length, geodesic, Minkowski, Lorentz or dist in any statement.

2 Definitions: CausallyCompact (Properties.lean:84), GloballyHyperbolic = IsCausal ∧ compact diamonds (:144), IsCausal (:95), HasTimeFunction (CurvesExtend.lean:518: ∃ T continuous, strictly increasing along ≤_M on distinct points) are the library's own definitions and the ladder's `lean` names. The proofs (Icc case split for compactness, le_antisymm via isolatedLine_le_top, T = id) are correct and kernel-checked. isolatedLine (LocateExtension.lean:512): x ≤_U y iff x = y ∈ U, or x < y and [x,y] ⊆ U ∖ {0}. isolatedLine_le_top (SCOpenWithoutTarentin.lean:260) says ≤_M ⊆ ≤ of ℝ. GH without tarentin is plausible and true: any diamond J(p,q) containing 0 forces p = q = 0, J(0,0) = {0} has empty interior, so tarentin fails at 0, while every diamond is [p,q], ∅ or {0}, hence compact. The four new names are unique (grep -w over all lean* packages, excluding .lake). None of the four facts existed before under any name.

2b Ladder steps cited in the docstring all exist as [[implies]] / [[fact]] rows: absolutely_minimal ∧ causally_plain ⇒ push_up [T1]; push_up ⇒ locally_push_up; causally_open ⇒ causally_open_future; causally_open_future ⇒ locally_causally_open_future; causally_open ⇒ locally_causally_open; strongly_causal ⇒ is_causal [T1]; fact curves_extend [T1, second_countable]. In a deleted probe, causal_ladder also derives isolatedLine.AbsolutelyMinimal from CausallyArcConnected, which bears out kb proposal 2.

3 Re-pointing: the entries are at programme/ladder.toml:1805 (fails[36], to tarentin) and :2029 (fails[51], to has_chronal_neighbour). The working copy equals HEAD 1b8e26a1. Each `from` id (causally_arc_connected, causally_plain, strongly_causal, strongly_causal_open, causally_open) is a conjunct (1–5), and ¬ Tarentin and ¬ HasChronalNeighbourEverywhere are conjuncts 18 and 19. In-memory simulation, deepcopy, ladder not written. (A) Re-pointing both witnesses to Causal.isolatedLine_separates leaves matrix() equal to baseline, with 0 _contradictions and 0 check errors when the new name is added to lean_names. Without the name, check reports the witness not found twice, so the re-point waits for graduation. (B) Adding globally_hyperbolic, causally_compact and time_function to both `from` leaves the matrix equal, with 0 contradictions and 0 errors. In (A), counterexample() gives each entry 13 `has` ids, all conjuncts. Its `lacks` are {tarentin, chronal_neighbours} and {has_chronal_neighbour, chronal_neighbours}, all negated conjuncts. Fails witnesses appear only in comments of Ladder/Test.lean and DualTest.lean, never as imports.

4 Finding: the comment at programme/ladder.toml:2530–2534 is quoted verbatim in the docstring (lines 41–45). 'none of which is in Lean' becomes stale at graduation. That is correct but incomplete, see the findings. J_M(0,0) = {0} and J_M(-1,1) = ∅ were proved in the audit probe.

findings.what: The docstring of isolatedLine_separates describes its conjunct ¬ isolatedLine.HasChronalNeighbourEverywhere as 'no chronal neighbour at `0`'. The statement says less: only that some point lacks a chronal neighbour. The stronger fact is true in the library (isolatedLine_not_hasChronalNeighbour_zero, LocateExtension.lean:623), but the theorem does not state it, and the docstring should say what is proved.
findings.fix: Write 'not every point has a chronal neighbour (0 has none, isolatedLine_not_hasChronalNeighbour_zero)'. Alternatively, add the conjunct ¬ isolatedLine.HasChronalNeighbour 0.

findings.what: The stale-comment finding is true but incomplete. The comment (written 2026-11-21, 7852b549) was already partly stale before this target. Since 2026-11-23 (364ec2d3, 791b0aa4) the isolated line has been strongly causal in Lean (isolatedLine_stronglyCausal, SCOpenWithoutTarentin.lean:273), hence causal on T1 spaces (StronglyCausal.isCausal, StrongCausality.lean:58). The → tarentin entry at :1805, whose `from` holds causally_plain and strongly_causal, already refutes causally_plain ∧ strongly_causal ⇒ tarentin and, through the closure, the is_causal form. Only causally_compact, globally_hyperbolic and time_function are new in Lean with this module. The 'J_M(0,0) = {0}' remark (proved in the audit probe) is a precision, not an error in the comment: the comment's own parenthetical '0 is related to itself only' gives it, and 'empty across 0' is right for p < q with 0 ∈ [p,q]. The REPORT words it as a precision. The dispatch's 'rather than empty' overstates it.
findings.fix: When the keeper rewrites :2530–2534, credit strong causality and causality to the 2026-11-23 witnesses and cite isolatedLine_separates only for causally_compact, globally_hyperbolic and time_function. Keep the J(0,0) = {0} remark as a precision, not as a correction.
